title: Independent Component Analysis (ICA)
interviewAnswer: ICA decomposes observed mixtures into latent components that are statistically independent, typically relying on non-Gaussianity; unlike PCA, the objective is independence rather than just uncorrelated variance directions.
why: ICA is a classic blind-source-separation method and deepens understanding of latent representations.
intuition: Multiple microphones record mixtures of the same speakers; ICA tries to recover the original independent sources.
deepDive: After centering/whitening, ICA optimizes a measure of non-Gaussianity or independence. Components are identifiable only up to permutation and scale/sign under standard assumptions.
commonMistakes: Assuming ICA can separate Gaussian sources uniquely.
production: Check component stability and physical interpretability; preprocessing strongly affects results.
workedExample: Separate mixed audio signals recorded by several sensors without knowing the mixing coefficients.
